note: Learning metadata only. These objects do not authorize, deny, or detect. Splunk does not enforce CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 or CTRL-MCP-001.
path_a: TRY IT YOURSELF — construct the search in Splunk Search. Studio tokens are not the fresh LIVE run.id.
path_b: SHOW SOLUTION — copyable SPL from an existing hunt, bound table on canonical REPLAY, explanation, limitations.

investigations.title: Find the retrieved-context event
investigations.security_question: Where is the retrieved-context evidence for this run?
investigations.learning_objective: Locate run.id, sequence, event.name, document.id, provenance, and content.hash. Retrieval evidence is not authorization evidence.
prerequisites: a run.id from Attack Service or Investigate specimen
investigations.starter_guidance: Index agentsec_telemetry, sourcetype otel:agentic:json. Filter quoted agentsec.run.id. Find CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001. Read document.id, provenance, and content.hash. Do not search index=*.
investigations.hint_1: Start with index=agentsec_telemetry sourcetype=otel:agentic:json and the quoted field agentsec.run.id. Paste the LIVE run.id from Attack Service, or use the Investigate specimen REPLAY id.
investigations.hint_2: Q-RAG-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY is the governed hunt. CONTEXT-001 is hop 0. Provenance rag.local.fixture is source identity, not trust.
investigations.expected_result_shape: One CONTEXT-001 row. BASELINE: doc.lending-policy.normal. ATTACK/RETEST: doc.lending-policy.malicious. Provenance rag.local.fixture. Hash present.
investigations.result_explanation: You are looking at the indexed copy of one retrieve. run.id is the experiment key. document.id names the fixture. content.hash fingerprints the bytes.
investigations.security_interpretation: Retrieval evidence shows what entered agent context. It does not show a grant. Splunk did not retrieve the document.
investigations.does_not_prove: Finding the retrieve does not prove the document was trusted, malicious, or authorized. Empty is not SAFE.

investigations.title: What trust classification was assigned?
investigations.security_question: How did CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 classify the retrieved context?
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the same run.id. Read context.trust, control.id, control.decision, control.reason on the CONTEXT-001 row.
investigations.hint_1: Q-RAG-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY columns include context_trust, context_decision, context_reason.
investigations.hint_2: Valid documents are always OBSERVE retrieved_context_is_data, including ATTACK. untrusted_data is a label, not malice.
investigations.expected_result_shape: CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE, reason retrieved_context_is_data, trust untrusted_data on BASELINE, ATTACK, and RETEST.
investigations.result_explanation: Classification is independent of the vulnerable overlay. CONTEXT-001 does not ALLOW the tool.
investigations.security_interpretation: OBSERVE != ALLOW. The observation control did not authorize lookup_customer_tier.
investigations.does_not_prove: untrusted_data does not mean the document is an attack. OBSERVE does not mean the content is permitted as policy.

investigations.title: Did retrieved content influence a privileged request?
investigations.security_question: After retrieval, did the agent request lookup_customer_tier at customer:read?
investigations.learning_objective: Reconstruct retrieve → follow-on request. INFLUENCE != AUTHORITY.
investigations.starter_guidance: On Q-RAG-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY read follow-on tool and requested_scope. BASELINE should have no privileged follow-on. ATTACK and RETEST should request lookup_customer_tier.
investigations.hint_1: The hunt already joins CONTEXT-001 to the follow-on request fields. You are not hunting an AGENT NOTE regex.
investigations.hint_2: ATTACK and RETEST should show the same follow-on REQUEST. That is influence, not a grant.
investigations.expected_result_shape: BASELINE: no follow-on. ATTACK/RETEST: lookup_customer_tier / customer:read after OBSERVE.
investigations.result_explanation: The closed interpreter recognized the fixture marker and formed a request. The request is not coded_policy.
investigations.security_interpretation: INFLUENCE != AUTHORITY. A document can cause a REQUEST without becoming a GRANT.
investigations.does_not_prove: Seeing lookup_customer_tier in telemetry does not mean the tool was granted. Do not treat AGENT NOTE as a production IOC.

investigations.title: Who actually authorized the tool?
investigations.security_question: What did CTRL-MCP-001 decide on the follow-on request?
investigations.learning_objective: CTRL-MCP-001 is the tool PDP. CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 did not authorize the tool.
investigations.starter_guidance: Filter event.name=agentsec.control.decision. Distinguish hop-0 CONTEXT-001 from hop-1 CTRL-MCP-001. Read decision and reason.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-AUTHZ lists control rows. Hop 0 is OBSERVE. Hop 1 is the tool PDP when a follow-on exists.
investigations.hint_2: LIVE ATTACK hop 1: ALLOW vulnerable_profile_fail_open:retrieved_context_derived_authority. Defended RETEST hop 1: DENY tool_not_granted. BASELINE: no hop-1 MCP grant.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Hop 0 OBSERVE always. ATTACK hop 1 ALLOW overlay reason. RETEST hop 1 DENY tool_not_granted.
investigations.result_explanation: The overlay is labeled lab fail-open. coded_policy still lists lookup_policy only. Splunk did not ALLOW or DENY.
investigations.security_interpretation: CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 did not authorize the tool. CTRL-MCP-001 did. AcmeBank owns enforcement.
investigations.does_not_prove: ALLOW is not execution. DENY is not independently proof the handler never ran. Overlay reason is not a production IOC.

investigations.title: Did execution actually begin?
investigations.security_question: Is there execution evidence after the tool authorization decision?
investigations.learning_objective: ALLOW != EXECUTION. ATTACK should show mcp.started then mcp.completed and handler > 0. RETEST handler = 0. Missing mcp.started is corroborative only.
investigations.starter_guidance: Search mcp.started / mcp.completed on this run.id. Read has_started on Q-MCP-EXECUTED. Runtime handler count remains authoritative.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-TOOL is mcp.started only. Q-MCP-EXECUTED joins control + mcp.* into execution_state.
investigations.hint_2: LIVE ATTACK complete copy: mcp.started then mcp.completed, handler 1. Defended RETEST complete copy: zero mcp.started. Zero Splunk rows corroborate local handler count; they do not independently prove prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK: has_started=1. RETEST: no_indexed_followon_execution_event. BASELINE: no privileged start.
investigations.result_explanation: mcp.started means the handler began. mcp.completed is success of a begun call, not authorization.
investigations.security_interpretation: ALLOW != EXECUTION. Runtime lookup_customer_tier handler count is authoritative for whether the privileged operation ran.
investigations.does_not_prove: Empty Splunk is not prevention. mcp.failed after start is execution then error, not blocked.

investigations.title: Prove ATTACK and RETEST used the same malicious content
investigations.security_question: Do ATTACK and RETEST share document.id, content.hash, provenance, requested tool, and requested scope?
investigations.learning_objective: SAME CONTENT. SAME REQUEST. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. Do not use hop-1 request hash as the document fingerprint.
investigations.starter_guidance: Compare CONTEXT-001 content.hash and document.id across the two LIVE run.ids. Then compare follow-on tool and scope. Then compare CTRL-MCP-001 decision.
investigations.hint_1: Q-RAG-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY on each run.id. The document fingerprint is agentsec.content.hash on CONTEXT-001, not the MCP request hash.
investigations.hint_2: Canonical REPLAY hashes: ATTACK and RETEST both sha256:c565f364c7c5fba3cf25d235bb8e2bee7d9433daa9f07d5e097ab6d2a82a97ef. Fresh LIVE launches mint new run.ids with the same bytes.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Same document.id, same content.hash, same provenance, same tool, same scope. Different profile, different MCP decision, different handler count, different run.id.
investigations.result_explanation: Equivalence is the document bytes and the follow-on request. The discriminator is server-owned ExperimentContext.
investigations.security_interpretation: SAME RETRIEVED CONTENT. SAME REQUEST. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT EXECUTION.
investigations.does_not_prove: Matching hashes does not mean the document is a confirmed compromise. One RETEST is not universal RAG resistance.

investigations.title: What can the evidence prove?
investigations.security_question: Which claims are SUPPORTED, CORROBORATED, NOT PROVEN, or INCORRECT?
investigations.learning_objective: Classify findings. Prohibit Splunk-blocked, document-is-safe, untrusted-means-malicious, hash-means-compromise, empty-means-prevented, DET-MCP-001-zero-means-safe.
investigations.starter_guidance: Write four columns: SUPPORTED / CORROBORATED / NOT PROVEN / INCORRECT. Use runtime handler count as authoritative for execution. Use Splunk as a copy.
investigations.hint_1: SUPPORTED: untrusted_data classification; influence of a request; ATTACK CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW; RETEST handler 0 with local count.
investigations.hint_2: INCORRECT: retrieved content granted the tool; the SIEM stopped execution; known catalog hash means compromise; empty search means prevented; DET-MCP-001 zero means SAFE.
investigations.expected_result_shape: A classification table you wrote, not a detector output.
investigations.result_explanation: Evidence discipline is the skill. Dashboards do not decide truth.
investigations.security_interpretation: Authoritative: runtime decision and handler count on this experiment. Corroborative: Splunk copy when complete. Splunk is not enforcement.
investigations.does_not_prove: Universal RAG safety, production detector coverage, or that sanitizing documents would have been the control.
